topics.topic: Disclosure class assigned to empty outputs of mapped operations
questions: Which disclosure class must an empty output list of a mapped operation carry?
Which class does an empty output list from a mapped operation receive when the binding's declared output class differs from the highest input class?
For a mapped operation over an empty list, does each empty output list take the binding output port's declared class or the highest class among the node's inputs?

quotes:
A binding output is not carried from the operation's inputs: it takes the
   class the binding declares, which the owner accepted with the binding (A08),
   whatever its inputs' classes — at proof time, at run time, and for the empty
   lists of a mapped operation over an empty list alike.

an empty list
   takes the highest class among the node's inputs — the list it mapped over
   and every other input — as an execution of the node would have received
   them (M21), so no class is lowered;
judgement.why: The two passages assign different disclosure classes to the same empty mapped-operation output when the binding output class differs from the inputs' highest class.

Does credential normalization remove one trailing LF byte, one trailing CRLF sequence, any Unicode newline, or all trailing newline sequences?

judgement.why: P3 judged the same trailing-newline normalization question on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Unit and truncation stage used for redacted failure-detail length
quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
precedent.why: The later note specifies the UTF-8 byte length of the retained failure_detail.

topics.topic: Which mapped-element execution outcomes are terminal conclusions versus retryable attempts
questions: Does “concluded element” mean any element having a NodeExecution, or only an element whose latest attempt has a terminal conclusion rather than a retryable wait?
Does `concluded record` mean any existing NodeExecution or only a NodeExecution whose combined element conclusion is terminal, and which retry rules take precedence?
Does “concluded record” mean any NodeExecution, or only a terminal element conclusion, and exactly which recorded waiting outcomes remain retryable?
Does a `service_unreachable` NodeExecution count as an element conclusion for deciding whether the mapped node has concluded, or is it a nonterminal attempt like unresolved `outcome_unknown`?

judgement.why: P14 judged the same scheduler finality and retry question for concluded and waiting elements on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Scheduler eligibility, semantic finality, and retry rules for concluded or waiting nodes and mapped elements
quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST read the Run by identity, its pinned graph with read_flow_version, and its trace with read_records through ExecutionsOfRun, and derive every element's conclusion from the trace: a function element from its NodeExecution's status, an operation element from operation_element_conclusion. If any NodeExecution of the run is refused_by_owner it reaches nothing and ends the run refused. Otherwise it executes one node at a time until no node can execute, then writes the rest or end state in one RecordRunProgressChange.

advance_run: [BEHAVIOR] A function element is executed with execute_function_element; an operation element is reached with reach_operation_element, given a RunContext of the run_id, the pinned flow_version_id and started_under the store_position of the FlowActivation read with ActivationBeforeRun, whose absence is raised as StoreInternalError; operation elements that wait are not reached again here.

operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Decides from the latest NodeExecution of the element, the one with the highest attempt_number, in this order: succeeded concludes succeeded with that record's outputs; outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied concludes succeeded with no outputs when the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; any status other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown concludes failed with that status and detail_code; then an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt resolved not_applied waits with reason owner_approval and no approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown; then service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable; with no NodeExecution and no requested approval the element is not reached.

advance_run: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text. A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element with no concluded record that does not wait, before the next node is selected; a waiting or failed element does not stop the elements after it, and a concluded element is never executed again.
precedent.why: The later run contract derives semantic conclusions from the trace, excludes waiting operation elements from ordinary advancement, forbids re-executing concluded elements, and classifies resolved `not_applied` as waiting for approval.

topics.topic: Disclosure class of executions with no classified inputs or outputs
questions: What class does an execution have when that set is empty, especially an inputless function failure or an operation with neither inputs nor outputs?
What disclosure class does an inputless function execution, or an operation execution with neither inputs nor outputs, have for trace and failure-detail disclosure?

judgement.why: P27 judged the same empty-set disclosure-class question on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Disclosure class for executions with no named inputs or outputs
quotes: highest_disclosure_class: [BEHAVIOR] MUST return the highest member of classes by the declared order of = models.DisclosureClass (open, then business_confidential, then personal_data) and open when classes is empty; no input ever lowers the result.
precedent.why: The later canonical-values contract assigns `open` when the set of execution input and output classes is empty.

topics.topic: Ordering of derived non-execution conclusions relative to executable nodes
questions: When a completed node simultaneously makes downstream nodes skipped or upstream_failed while independent nodes are ready, are all derived conclusion records written immediately before another executable node is selected, or are derived conclusions interleaved with executable nodes by node_id?
When some nodes are ready to execute while others can now be concluded without execution, which event happens first and therefore receives the earlier store position and timestamp?

judgement.why: P4 judged the same ordering question for derived non-execution records on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Ordering of derived skip and upstream-failure records relative to executable nodes
quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] After each function element MUST write one RecordRunProgressChange holding that element's execution, its StoredValues and SpooledFiles, and every skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed record that became determined, executions sorted by (node_id, map_index), with status running; after an operation element, whose concluding record effects wrote, the next RecordRunProgressChange holds the records it made non-executable.
precedent.why: The later run contract requires newly determined skipped and upstream-failed records to be written immediately after the element that determined them, before the advancement loop selects another executable node.

topics.topic: Release-specific size limit used for historical mapped-node aggregate failures
questions: Which release's stored_value_bytes_max is used to re-derive an old mapped node's aggregate failure after an upgrade, since the run records do not name a release or ceiling and recorded executions must not be reinterpreted?
Which release's `stored_value_bytes_max` governs derivation of an unfinished or historical mapped node after an upgrade?

quotes: when its canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant nothing is written and the node is failed for its dependants, which conclude upstream_failed, every element record staying as it is;
judgement.why: The later run contract directs every derivation to use the release constant imported by the running release.

Besides having all inputs, which node states are eligible for selection: must the node have no terminal conclusion and no waiting point, and how does an approval, resolution, or resume make it eligible again?

topics.topic: Whether credential non-disclosure covers encoded representations or only exact values
questions: Must the kernel uphold the State 0 guarantee for encoded representations of credentials, or is the guarantee limited to a verbatim credential byte sequence?
Must the kernel guarantee that encoded representations of a credential never enter records or responses, or is the prohibition limited to the exact credential value/byte sequence?

quotes:
- **Secrets** — service credentials and tokens live in the installation's
  protected configuration; they never enter a function, a flow, a trace or an
  answer.

A service's own answer is not the
   kernel's text: a body that echoes the value verbatim, 2xx or not, is
   withheld and never used as an output (A09 rule 7); one that carries it in
   another encoding is not recognised, and is protected only by its class.
judgement.why: State 0 prohibits credentials from entering any answer, while State 2 permits an encoded representation to be retained and disclosed according to its class.

topics.topic: Behavior when the configured instance name is absent from the manifest
questions: What happens when configuration selects a non-existent instance name: does the kernel refuse to start, treat the service as having no selected instance, or treat it as an instance with a missing address when proposing or invoking a binding?

topics.topic: Durable representation of a mapped-node aggregate-size failure
questions: What exact durable fact lets every reader distinguish this aggregate-size failure from other mapped-node failures and report its reason after release or restart, given that no NodeExecution records it?

topics.topic: Durable representation of the disclosure class of an empty mapped file list
questions: Where is the disclosure class of an empty mapped file output represented durably so it can be recovered and delivered after restart?

topics.topic: Security checks applied when rereading a configuration file changed after startup
questions: If the configuration file is replaced after startup by a symlink, a file owned by another user, or a group-readable file, must token re-reading reject every request or accept the new token list after only A16's four checks?

topics.topic: Syntax, address-family support, and exposure checks for the MCP listen address
questions: What syntax denotes this address, which address families are allowed, and what startup checks or exposure restrictions apply?

topics.topic: Whether proof-time disclosure propagation accounts for correlations between mutually exclusive guards
questions: Does proof compute the maximum class over every structurally possible source without considering guard correlations, or may mutually exclusive guard values narrow the class that can reach a function in one execution?
